h: Wetlands, drag racing and a Northamptonshire day out
p: A climbing session is a good way to start a day at Rushden Lakes, because energy levels are high and queues tend to be shorter earlier on. Arrive a little before your slot so harnesses and the safety talk don't eat into your climbing time. Trainers with good grip, comfy clothes and short nails all make the walls a bit easier to tackle.

Rushden Lakes sits alongside the Nene Wetlands nature reserve, and the Wildlife Trust has a visitor centre on site where you can learn about the birds and wildlife that live around the lakes and river. Walking trails lead out into the reserve, so it's easy to swap the climbing walls for some proper fresh air. Bring binoculars if you have them; there's often plenty to spot on the water.

Just next door, Higham Ferrers is a small historic market town with a lovely old church, medieval buildings and a peaceful market square, great for a quiet wander. Irchester Country Park, a short drive away, has woodland walks and play areas for younger children. Motorsport fans may know that Santa Pod Raceway, the famous drag racing venue, is only a few miles away near Podington, with events through the season. Whichever way you round off the day, Rushden makes a good base for exploring this corner of Northamptonshire, and the A45 makes it easy to reach from Northampton, Wellingborough and further afield.
